title: Nominalization
summary: Turn actions into nouns to create concise academic, journalistic, and professional Portuguese.

sections.heading: From verb to noun
sections.body: Nominalization turns a process into a noun phrase. It is common in formal writing because it lets writers discuss actions as concepts, causes, or results.

examples.pt: A redução dos gastos gerou debate.
examples.en: The reduction in spending generated debate.

sections.heading: Common endings
sections.body: Portuguese uses endings such as **-ção**, **-mento**, **-agem**, **-ncia**, and **-dade**. The best noun is lexical, not always predictable.

examples.note: both exist with different preferences by context

sections.heading: Avoiding heavy prose
sections.body: Nominalization can make writing concise, but too many abstract nouns make sentences dense. Mix nominal and verbal style for clarity.

examples.pt: A implementação da proposta depende da aprovação do conselho.
examples.en: Implementation of the proposal depends on board approval.

examples.pt: Para implementar a proposta, o conselho precisa aprová-la.
examples.en: To implement the proposal, the board needs to approve it.
There was an increase in demand.

keyPoints: Nominalization is central to formal and academic Portuguese.
Nominal style can hide agents; verbal style often improves clarity.
Choose established nouns rather than inventing forms.

commonMistakes.wrong: A análise dos dados foram importantes.
commonMistakes.right: A análise dos dados foi importante.
commonMistakes.note: The head noun análise is singular.

commonMistakes.wrong: Excessive nominalizations always sound more advanced.
commonMistakes.right: Use nominalizations when they add precision or cohesion.
